title: Exchange cells with a push: orientation, small deviations, mutual costs

key_results.statement: $J>0$, field alone, every $S$, cubic torus or ring of even side: the lowest eigenvector is unique, a total-spin singlet, unchanged by every common rotation, with $\langle\mathbf S_x\rangle=0$ (exact).
$J<0$, field alone: lowest eigenvalue $JS^2DN$, $(2NS+1)$-fold degenerate; no lowest eigenvector is unchanged by all common rotations (exact).

$J<0$ with the push: the product state is the unique lowest eigenvector and $\langle\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S_x\rangle=S$ exactly for every $x$, $L$, $S$, $h_p>0$, both graphs and both orders of limits.
$J>0$, order $h_p\to0$ at fixed $L$, then $L\to\infty$: $m(x)=O(h_p)\to0$ for every $S$ on both graphs (exact).

The expansion on which Assumption E rests: at leading order in $1/S$ about the orientation set by the push, $C=E_0+\frac12\sum_{\alpha=1,2}q^{(\alpha)T}(JS\Delta+h_pP_h)q^{(\alpha)}+O(J)$ with $q^{(\alpha)}_x=\epsilon_x\mathbf e_\alpha\cdot\mathbf S_x/\sqrt S$, $[q^{(1)}_x,q^{(2)}_y]=i\epsilon_x\delta_{xy}$; the quartic remainder is of relative order $1/S$ while $\langle n_x\rangle\ll S$.

Under Assumption E, its condition $\langle n_x\rangle\ll S$ with the push requires $Nh_{\rm eff}S\gg zJ$, with $h_{\rm eff}=(1/h_p+\hat g_L(0)/(JS))^{-1}$ the restoring coefficient of the collective rotation lowered by the relaxation near the push ($h_p/(1+\eta\gamma_3)$ on the cubic torus as $L\to\infty$); equivalently $Nh_pS\gg zJ$ and $NS^2\gg z\hat g_L(0)$; met in the order $L\to\infty$ first (on the ring if $S^2\gg\frac16$), violated in the order $h_p\to0$ at fixed $L$.

Under Assumption E, cubic torus, $J>0$, order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$, then $h_p\to0$: $m(x)\to\epsilon_h[S-\Delta S_3+O(1/S)]$ with $\Delta S_3=\frac12[\int(1-\gamma_k^2)^{-1/2}-1]=0.0784$, independent of $h_p>0$; the expansion at fixed $L$ is taken at fixed $\eta=h_p/(JS)$, where the collective rotation adds $\frac12\sqrt{2zJS/(Nh_{\rm eff})}\,w_{\rm far}$ at the far place, with $w_{\rm far}=1-2\eta_{\rm eff}\hat g_L(\text{far}-h)+O(\eta_{\rm eff}^2/L^2)$, $\eta_{\rm eff}=h_{\rm eff}/(JS)$, a finite-size correction of relative order $\eta_{\rm eff}/L$ since $\hat g_L(\text{far}-h)=O(1/L)$; at fixed $h_p$ and $L$ only $m=S-\frac12\sqrt{2zJS/(Nh_p)}+O(S^0)$ is stated (collective rotation, $h_{\rm eff}=h_p[1+O(1/S)]$ there), and both collective terms vanish as $L\to\infty$, so the limit holds in either scaling.

Under Assumption E, ring (control): $m(R)=S-\frac1\pi\ln R+O(1)+O(1/S)$; the first correction is not uniform in $R$ and the expansion in $1/S$ does not decide the order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$ at any $S$.

Exact diagonalization ($S=\frac12$ rings $L\le20$ and one 16-object cubic cluster, $S=1$ rings $L\le12$), all sectors of $\sum_xS^3_x$ searched, at the sampled $h_p/J=0.01,0.1,0.3,1,3,10$: the lowest eigenvector is unique and lies in $M=0$; $m_{\rm far}$ is linear in $h_p$ at the two smallest strengths and on rings with $h_p\ge J$ decreases with $L$; for $S=\frac12$ on the cubic torus the order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$ is undecided at these sizes.

Under Assumption E, identification at leading order in $1/S$: two conjugate copies $q^{(\alpha)}$ with the 05-anchor matrix $A=JS\Delta+h_pP_h$, $\kappa_h=JS$, $\kappa_a=h_p$, $g_s=\epsilon_{x_s}\sqrt S g(\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf e_\alpha)$, exact for the static results of the quadratic expansion; kinetic matrix $EAE$ instead of $\mathbb 1$; separately, for dynamics, the long-wavelength model: two copies of the 05-anchor field with $\frac12p^2$, $\kappa_h=2zJ^2S^2$, $g_s=\epsilon_{x_s}S\sqrt{2zJ}g(\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf e_\alpha)$ and the anchor $\kappa_a=2zJSh_p$ matched to the exact static result, without local momentum terms (these would give the static anchor $\kappa_a/(1+\eta/(2z))$); its static results with linear sources are exact for every $\eta$ and $L$; for dynamics, on the cubic torus with $L\to\infty$ first, it holds at $k\ll1$ for every $\eta$, with a local error at $h$ of relative order $k$ (odd in frequency, coupling the copies) and a bulk error of relative order $k^2$; on the ring only its static statements are derived, as the question's note of 2026-10-26 (after the review of v5) asks.
Under Assumption E, conditions of (8.10): $\Delta S_3\ll S$, $Nh_{\rm eff}S\gg zJ$ (8.6), $|g|\ll h_p$, $|g|\ll JS$; on the ring also $\frac1\pi\ln d\ll S$ and $|g|d\ll JS$ at the distances used.

Under (8.10), (8.11) and Assumption E: (5.3) with the anchor, (5.8), (5.10), (5.11), (5.14), (5.15) hold, unbounded outcomes become bounded rotations of the orientation, and the next order in $1/S$ changes coefficients by relative $O(1/S)$; exact (A1, (8.1)): the outcome no lowest eigenvector of (5.3)–(5.6) fails because one exists.

Under Assumption E, transverse direction sources, order $g_1g_2$, leading order in $1/S$, every $L$, both graphs: $\mathcal E^\perp_{12}=-S\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp)G_a(x_1,x_2)$.

Under Assumption E, cubic torus, order $L\to\infty$, distances to $h\to\infty$, then $r\to\infty$, $r$ the midpoint separation: separation part $-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp)c_{\rm cell}/(4\pi Jr)+O(r^{-3})$ with $c_{\rm cell}=c_1c_2$ ($c_i=1$ single object, $2$ two-object cell): a long-range mark of order $S^0$; it vanishes for a source at $h$ or $\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp=0$.

Under Assumption E, along-$\mathbf n$ direction sources: mutual cost $-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1\cdot\mathbf n)(\mathbf m_2\cdot\mathbf n)c_1c_2\kappa_\parallel/(JSr^3)[1+O(r^{-2})]$, $r$ the midpoint separation, $\kappa_\parallel=\sqrt3/(16\pi^3)$, order $g_1g_2/(JS)$: no long-range mark.

Under Assumption E, changed link (R2), separation along an axis: $-\frac{\sqrt3}{8\pi^3}\frac{\delta_1\delta_2S}{Jr^7}a$ with $a=\frac{43}6+\frac52\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(\mathbf e_1\cdot\mathbf e_2)$ (both links parallel to $\mathbf r$), $\frac43-\frac5{12}\epsilon_1\epsilon_2(\mathbf e_1\cdot\mathbf e_2)$ (both perpendicular, parallel to each other), $\frac1{12}$ (both perpendicular, perpendicular to each other), $-\frac12$ (one parallel, one perpendicular); attractive for $\delta_1\delta_2>0$ except in the last case; $\epsilon_i$ is the class of the endpoint $x$ of link $i$ and $\mathbf e_i$ points from $y$ to $x$, and $a$ does not depend on which endpoint is called $x$; no pair has a vanishing coefficient; no long-range mark.

Under Assumption E, held spin (R1), leading order in $1/S$, $|g'|/J$, $|g'|s_b/(JS)$: $\mathcal E^{R1}_{12}=-\frac{|g'_1g'_2|\kappa_\parallel}{JSr^3}\int_0^\infty du\,e^{-u}\frac{u^2(s_{b_1}s_{b_2}u^2-\sigma_1\sigma_2\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}\beta_1\beta_2)}{(u^2+\beta_1^2)(u^2+\beta_2^2)}$, $\beta_i=2r/\ell_{b_i}$, $\ell_b=\sqrt{2z}J/|g'|$, $\sigma_i=-s_{b_i}{\rm sgn}\,g'_i$; for $1\ll r\ll\ell_b$ it is $-|g'_1g'_2|s_{b_1}s_{b_2}\kappa_\parallel/(JSr^3)[1+O(r/\ell_b)]$; for $r\gg\ell_b$ (the law for $r\to\infty$ last) $\frac{3\sqrt3}{8\pi^3}\frac JS\sigma_1\sigma_2\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}r^{-5}[1+O(\ell_b^2/r^2)]$; the momentum part of the propagators adds a term that vanishes iff $\epsilon_{x_1}\ne\epsilon_{x_2}$ or ${\rm sgn}(\sigma_1)\Delta_1+{\rm sgn}(\sigma_2)\Delta_2=0$ and otherwise lies within the remainders; near the zero $r_0$ of the integral the remainders are absolute, $s_{b_1}s_{b_2}[O(r^{-2})+O(1/S)+O(|g'|/J)+O(|g'|s_b/(JS))]$; no long-range mark.

Without a push, under Assumption E, cubic torus, $L\to\infty$ first, $|g_i|\ll JS$, $\mathbf h_i=c_ig_i\epsilon_{x_i}\mathbf m_i$: the orientation minimizes $E(\hat{\mathbf n})$; the mutual cost has the separation-independent part $S(|\mathbf h_1|+|\mathbf h_2|-|\mathbf h_{\rm eff}|)+O(\gamma_3|\mathbf h|^2/J)$ from the shared orientation (degree one, not analytic in the strengths) and the separation part $-\mathbf h_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf h_2^\perp/(4\pi Jr)+O(r^{-2})$ at the minimum; non-parallel $\mathbf m_i$, every ratio: unique orientation in the plane of $\mathbf m_1,\mathbf m_2$, separation part $+\tau_1^2/(4\pi Jr)[1+O(\gamma_3|\mathbf h|/(JS))]>0$ (repulsive), with $\hat{\mathbf n}\simeq-\hat{\mathbf h}_{\rm eff}$ for non-cancelling sources; parallel $\mathbf m_i$: $-h_1h_2(1-u^{*2})/(4\pi Jr)$, $u^*=\min(1,SJH/Q)$, zero for $H\ge H_c=Q/(SJ)$, repulsive below; exact (Lieb–Mattis): relation sources fix no orientation.

open_issues: For S = 1/2 on the cubic torus the persistence of the orientation far from the push is undecided: one cluster of 16 objects.
On the ring the methods used do not decide m(x) far from the push; exact diagonalization only shows a decrease with L for L ≤ 20.
The next order in 1/S of (8.13)–(8.18) is not computed; survival of the 1/r law of (8.14) at all orders is not proven.
The corrections near the push to (8.16)–(8.18) are not computed; (8.17) is classified only for separations along an axis.

Without a push, for non-parallel sources near cancellation the orientation is the minimum of a one-variable function, not given in closed form; its uniqueness, its plane and the repulsive sign of the separation part are derived.
On the ring the dynamical range of the long-wavelength model is not derived; only its static statements are, as the question's note of 2026-10-26 (after the review of v5) asks.
The rotor regime N h_eff S ~ zJ between the two orders of item 1(b) is not computed; at fixed L and fixed h_p the remainder of order S^0 of the collective rotation is estimated, not computed.
The local terms at the push of the dynamical dictionary beyond the static matching (relative order k, odd in frequency) are bounded but not computed.

consistency_checks.check: S → ∞ of item 1(b): m/S → 1, the product state with staggered orientation; exact product state for J < 0
Identification against (5.15): 4πr ĝ_∞(r) → 1 on the lattice; R2 vertex summed over link directions equals the energy density of the copy
Dimensions and S-scaling of all mutual costs: (vertex)² / (level spacing JS)
